Subject: Logging redaction acceptance criteria — post-demo recap

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for your time on the demo today — appreciated the candid discussion on how MedTech handles PHI in telemetry. Per our call, I wanted to summarize the proposed acceptance criteria for Redwood logs (request/response + header-level data) so your security/procurement teams can review quickly. This is meant to be a concise checklist we can sign off on before moving to a pilot.

High-level proposed acceptance criteria:
- PII redaction: request/response bodies must be configurable to mask/omit fields matching configurable JSON paths and regex rules (examples: patient_name, ssn, mrn).
- Header hygiene: downstream-sensitive headers (Authorization, X-Trace-ID) must be redacted or replaced at the gateway; trace IDs should be pseudonymized so they cannot be correlated to raw IDs.
- Retention controls: ingestion window configurable per environment (30/90/365 days) and irreversible deletion upon retention expiration.
- Access controls: role-based access to raw logs with audit trail; no raw PHI in logs for hosted PII profiles.
- Evidence & verification: delivery of redaction-checklist-v1.pdf and SOC2-summary.xlsx as initial artifacts; live demo of a redaction run on a sample dataset.

Attachments: redaction-checklist-v1.pdf (detailed mapping), SOC2-summary.xlsx (summary controls).

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm which of the above are "must have" vs "nice to have" for the pilot.
2) Redwood provides a short runbook + sample dataset for the redaction demo (we'll coordinate with Karthik).
3) Procurement sends any standard security addendum/contract items we should review.

If useful, Karthik can scope the engineering work (effort estimate + timeline) once we get a prioritized list.

Quick ask: can you confirm who from MedTech's security/engineering will be the primary technical contact? Tom or someone else?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao

aditya@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

- Must haves for pilot: PII redaction (configurable rules), header hygiene (Authorization must be removed), and retention controls (configurable with proof of deletion).
- Nice to have: per-route pseudonymization of trace IDs (we need to understand collision/resolution behavior).
- Evidence: the two attachments look good as a starting point. We will need a short run showing redaction applied to a realistic payload (non-production copy).

Primary technical contact: that's me for security questions; I'll loop in our infra lead (cc'd Tom for procurement now). For engineering QA we also expect a short run with our dev team to verify no disruption to observability.

2) Can Redwood redact at both key-level (JSON path) and token-level (regex)? We have some free-text notes we need to clean.

Happy to take a short technical note — or Karthik can call into a 30-min session with our infra lead to go over specifics.

Subject: Re: Logging redaction acceptance criteria — post-demo recap

Laura — thanks, that prioritization is exactly what we needed. Quick answers and next-step suggestion below.

Q1 (pseudonymization): by default Redwood offers deterministic pseudonymization for trace IDs (SHA-256-based keyed hash with customer-specific key). Output is non-reversible by Redwood without the key; we can either use a customer-managed key (KMS) or Redwood-managed key per your preference. Deterministic hashing preserves the ability to correlate requests internal to a session while preventing exposure of the original ID.

Q2 (redaction granularity): yes — we support both JSON-path keyed redaction and regex-based token redaction. For free-text fields we recommend a two-pass approach: first apply token-level regex for known patterns (SSN, MRN), then apply ML-based PII detection for residual free text (we can configure thresholds so you control false positives).

Proposed short plan:
- Karthik will run a short engineering session (30 min) with your infra lead to confirm regex examples and the sample dataset format.
- Redwood provides a temporary test endpoint and the redaction demo runbook (we'll share a link to a hosted doc and the small sample payload).
- After the demo, we'll deliver the evidence package (redaction log + before/after snapshots) and an auditor-friendly summary.

I've attached the redaction-checklist-v1.pdf as requested. Karthik — can you confirm availability for a 30-min call tomorrow morning Pacific? Also note we may need to surface any performance impact on KV-cache or latency when applying ML PII detectors; capture rough token-level overhead so MedTech can plan SLOs.

Tom — looping you on the plan so procurement sees timing for the pilot and evidence delivery.

Thanks,
Aditya

Hi all — thanks for the clear priorities. I ran a quick review with engineering to validate the feasibility and to flag a couple of technical notes for the pilot acceptance criteria:

1) Trace ID pseudonymization: we will implement a keyed hash (HMAC-SHA256) by default; when MedTech opts for customer-managed KMS we will use the provided key for deterministic hashing. This is non-reversible from Redwood without the KMS key. Expected work: ~3 engineering days to add KMS key configuration to the redaction pipeline and ~1 day to add test coverage.

2) JSON-path + regex redaction: supported. We will provide a sample ruleset and a small CLI tool to validate rules against the sample payloads. Expected work: ~2 engineering days to expose ruleset UI + ~1 day for CLI/test harness.

3) ML-based PII detection: this is optional for the pilot. If you want ML detection, there is a token-level overhead we should measure in the demo — anticipate +5–12% token processing time depending on sequence length. We will capture latency numbers during the run.

4) Audit evidence: we will produce before/after snapshots (sanitized) and a redaction-log containing rule hits (no raw PIIs). For the retention proof, we can provide a deletion report that shows the retention policy was applied and objects expired; irreversible deletion will be demonstrated in the sandbox environment.

Suggested timeline: 2 business days to prepare test endpoint + runbook, 1 business day for the demo and evidence capture, then a 1–2 day wrap-up for the evidence package.

Action items (owner):
- Aditya: confirm pilot start date and agree who will provide the sample payload (MedTech).
- Laura: confirm KMS preference (Redwood-managed vs customer-managed).
- Tom: if procurement has standard contract addenda we should review now, please share.
- Karthik: schedule the 30-min technical session (I have an opening 04/26 09:00 PT).

I'll take the engineering ownership on the demo run. If helpful I can also include a short sequence diagram for how trace IDs are transformed and where redaction runs in the request flow.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
